entry.title: How ChatGPT Works (Simple Explanation for Beginners)
entry.summary:
If you’ve ever wondered what happens when you type a prompt into ChatGPT, this article breaks it down in the simplest way possible. Let’s go step by step User Input → Input Processing → Context Building → LLM → Output Processing → Response
When you enter a prompt: Your input is cleaned and structured Previous chat history is added Text is converted into tokens (numbers the model understands) Tokens are not always full words—they can be parts of words, spaces, or punctuation. Before sending your input to the model, the system adds extra information: Hidden system prompts (rules like “be helpful and safe”) App-level instructions (tone, format) Sometimes external data This helps guide how the AI should respond. The request is sent to a Large Language Model (LLM). The model: Reads the full context (input + history + system instructions) Generates a response token by token
Uses probability to predict the next word Important: It doesn’t “think” like a human—it predicts patterns. Before showing the result: Safety filters are applied Formatting is adjusted (like Markdown) The response is finalized [You] ↓ [Input Processing] ↓ [Context + Hidden Instructions] ↓ [LLM (Prediction Engine)] ↓ [Output Filtering & Formatting] ↓ [Final Response]
Real-world systems like ChatGPT can also include: Tool usage (APIs, calculators) Retrieval systems (fetching external knowledge) Memory layers This is a simplified mental model to get started. Understanding this helps you: Write better prompts Debug AI responses Build your own AI applications In the next post, I’ll explain how these models are actually created—from tokens to training to alignment.

Why multi-agent tracking is a new problem
Tracking one long-running task is easy. You can watch the terminal, or use a shell trick: # Play a bell sound when the last command finishes long-running-comman``d; afplay /System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff

Codex is CLI-first. There's no standard. You don't always know which agent is the bottleneck. If three are running, the one that finishes first might free you to continue — but which is it?
